findings.cause: The analyzer uses split(/s+/) rather than split(/\s+/) for bibliographic targets. The sealed oracle permits a bibliographic target followed by whitespace metadata, so the subject disagrees with its own independent semantic contract.
findings.why_load_bearing: The deterministic suite can be GREEN while a simple declared reference shape fails the sealed oracle. Therefore its candidate census and test closure are incomplete.

findings.cause: The analyzer trims each slash-delimited part independently and admits whitespace adjacent to the scope separator; the oracle's independently declared shape rejects it.
findings.why_load_bearing: The base test does not exercise the analyzer/oracle semantic seam even though the subject represents the oracle as its independent arbiter.

findings.cause: After an underline is consumed for a Setext heading, the next loop iteration reuses that same underline as another heading's content line. The oracle independently repeats the same non-consuming line loop, so it accepts the fabrication.
findings.expected: The underline line is consumed by the first Setext production and cannot become the content line of a second heading.

findings.cause: Both implementations copy raw attribute source text and never apply HTML character-reference decoding before semantic URL or definition-scope use. Raw byte provenance and decoded semantic value are distinct requirements; preserving only the raw spelling is insufficient.
findings.why_load_bearing: The required parsed-attribute provenance and relative URL relations cannot be exact across the pinned corpus if source entities are treated as literal URL/scope bytes.

findings.cause: Text URL discovery checks only lowercase literal schemes even though URL schemes are ASCII case-insensitive. Both analyzer and oracle share the same literal check.

findings.contract: The V9 blueprint names containers as a required single-stream consumer and requires heading, container, definition, and operation ownership to use both byte order and nesting.
findings.cause: The analyzer assigns every explicit algorithm to the globally preceding heading by byte offset. It emits no container relation and does not restore the outer heading when a nested section closes. The oracle repeats a global preceding-heading search.

reproduction.expected_structural_owner: the outer heading/container context after </section>, not the closed nested section's heading

findings.why_load_bearing: A content-addressed ledger can be made to agree with a source-derived owner that is itself structurally false. Exact locator and owner equality therefore do not prove the required nesting relation.

total_tranche.analysis: Repair2 makes material progress over a line-collapsed or regex-fabricated corpus inventory: exact UTF-8 intervals, raw-state coordinates, duplicate-interval ledger rejection, disposition totality, and collision rejection are real. It nevertheless cannot freeze the July-2026 CSS denominator because the occurrence census still misses admitted reference forms, shares semantic defects with its oracle, and violates the blueprint's container-aware ownership law. Using it to materialize 168-source rows now would content-address false headings, URLs, scopes, and owners and amplify rework downstream.

wave.analysis: Syntax, deterministic replay, external-CWD replay, the declared suite, and several hostile seams are GREEN. The wave fails its semantic close because exact counterexamples defeat both analyzer/oracle agreement and shared semantic correctness outside the suite. The correct next action is a bounded repair generation and two fresh exact-byte reviews, not a full-corpus run or shard publication.

Keep all formal cost, full-denominator, parser, and production credit at zero until the existing blueprint gates are independently proven.
